Subject: Sizing ask: committed capacity and latency fit for Velox POC

Rafael —

Thanks again for the demo. As we head toward a commercial commitment, procurement asked for a short technical summary mapping our expected traffic to Redwood Dedicated sizing and what headroom we should reserve for SLA compliance. High-level notes from our side:
- Expected steady queries: ~22M tokens/day (from baseline telemetry).
- Peak burst profile: ~3.2k tokens/sec over 4–6 minute windows (observed from beta).
- Target p95 generation latency: <= 250ms for customer-facing flows (single-turn).
- Model: production variant of Velox Llama-13B (we plan to use quantized 8-bit).

Can you summarize recommended GPU slab, recommended committed GPUs, and fallback options (e.g., smaller model or autoscale) we should include in the SOW? Ideally a few lines plus any numbers for tokens/sec per-GPU assumptions so procurement can match cost to capacity.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Infrastructure, Velox AI

Alex —

Appreciate the clear numbers. Attached is a short spreadsheet with the token profile you sent (velox_token_profile.csv) and a one-page recommendation (redwood_dedicated_recommendation_v1.pdf). High-level summary below — I kept the math explicit for procurement:

Summary (short):
- Assumptions: Llama-13B quantized 8-bit, 512 avg sequence length on generative flows, single-turn RPCs. Measured baseline: ~780 tokens/sec per A10x GPU at p95 <=250ms when batched to 8 concurrent requests (our lab profile).
- Customer peak: 3,200 tokens/sec observed -> baseline compute need = 3,200 / 780 = 4.1 GPUs.
- Headroom: 30% operational buffer recommended for burst runways, warm caches, and gradual traffic growth -> 4.1 * 1.30 = 5.3 -> round to 6 GPUs committed.
- Auto-burst/overflow: Allow Dedicated pool to burst to an additional 2 GPUs (on-demand) or configure fallback to a quantized-4bit 13B variant which gives ~40% higher tokens/sec per GPU (estimated) but may reduce sample fidelity.
- Latency mapping: at 6 committed GPUs, expected p95 gen latency <= 230ms in steady-state with prefix caching enabled; at 4 GPUs p95 risk rises toward 320ms during sustained bursts (no warm cache).

Implication for SOW language (proposal bullet):
- Commit: 6 A10x GPUs (reserved) to meet observed burst profile and p95 <=250ms with 30% operational headroom.
- Burst: configurable burst pool of +2 GPUs for 10-minute windows (pay-as-you-go).
- Fallback: automatic model-variant fallback to llm-13b-4q under sustained capacity pressure (quality regression threshold to be accepted by Velox).

Attaching the two artifacts and copying Ben and Priyom for pricing and ops confirmation. Happy to convert this to a one-paragraph SOW blurb for procurement.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Strategic Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Ben / Raf — checked our lab runs quickly: 780 tokens/sec per A10x at p95 is in the right ballpark for 8-bit 13B with batch=8 and seq=512; caveat: if real-world average seq length climbs above 700 tokens (Velox mentioned 512 avg, but they have long-code completion flows), throughput drops roughly 18–25%. Also note that prefix KV cache warm-up materially improves p95 for repeated prompts (observed 15–20% p95 improvement after warm cache).

Recommendation tweak: keep Rafael's 6 GPU commitment but include a clause that we will re-baseline after 30 days of production telemetry; if average seq length or burst cadence materially deviates, we will propose a mid-term adjustment. Also recommend a short canary period where we reserve 4 GPUs and enable automatic burst/overflow so Velox can validate traffic shape before payment ramp.

Priyom
Senior Compute Systems — Redwood Inference

Alex —

Thanks for the ask — Rafael and team summarized this cleanly. Couple of practical SOW bullets we often include that you might want to accept up front:
- 30 day re-baseline: Redwood will re-evaluate committed slab after 30 days of production telemetry and propose any changes (no unilateral changes without customer consent).
- Canary phase: start with 4 reserved GPUs + automatic burst to +2 GPUs for 14 days; if production telemetry matches your baseline we transition to the 6 GPU committed band (and apply the committed discount).
- Runbook: include a short operational runbook for degraded quality (model-fallback policy, contact on-call, and expected failover timings).

If that all reads OK we can produce an SOW paragraph and a draft contract exhibit for procurement to review. Rafael — please attach the one-pager as a finalized SOW blurb and I will route to contracts.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
